# Best AI Productivity Tools in 2026: Notion AI vs ClickUp AI vs Todoist AI

Most productivity tool comparisons miss the real question: where does your work already live? The best AI assistant is the one that sits inside the app you open all day, because the value comes from context, not from a clever model you have to copy text into. Notion AI, ClickUp AI, and Todoist AI each win on that basis, and the rest of the stack fills the gaps they leave.

## Notion AI: productivity inside your workspace

[[link:/tools/5|Notion AI]] (Freemium) is embedded in Notion, so it summarizes docs, answers questions, and fills properties using your workspace context without app-switching. Its strength is relevance: answers draw on the notes and pages you already keep. The limit is that it only helps if your knowledge actually lives in Notion, and access can require a VPN in some regions. If your team does not use Notion, this tool adds little.

## ClickUp AI: productivity inside your project tool

[[link:/tools/52|ClickUp AI]] (Freemium) integrates AI into ClickUp workflows, turning meeting discussions into summaries and trackable action items. It is most useful for teams already managing projects in ClickUp; outside that, its value drops. Access can require a VPN in some regions, and heavy use benefits from a paid plan.

## Todoist AI and its gap

Todoist AI is a popular task manager, but it is not listed in this directory, so we cannot link to it here. For users who live in a task list, the practical move is to pair it with capture and meeting tools rather than expect one app to cover notes, docs, and summaries. The tools below fill that gap without duplicating your task list.

## Notes, decks, and capture

[[link:/tools/87|Gamma]] (Freemium) generates first-draft decks from prompts with one-click theming, though complex layouts need manual tweaks. [[link:/tools/88|Tome]] (Freemium) builds structured narratives for pitches, less suited to dense data. [[link:/tools/243|Mem]] (Freemium) self-organizes notes and resurfaces ideas, while [[link:/tools/245|Obsidian]] (Freemium) keeps notes as local Markdown with bidirectional links, at the cost of a steeper setup. [[link:/tools/14|Obsidian Copilot]] (Freemium) grounds answers in your own vault but needs a model provider to function.

## Meetings and commands

[[link:/tools/1106|Fireflies AI]] (Freemium) transcribes and summarizes across conferencing platforms, though recording requires consent and advanced features need a paid plan. [[link:/tools/240|Sembly AI]] (Freemium) joins calls and tracks actions, though transcription drops with noisy audio. [[link:/tools/101|Raycast AI]] (Freemium) puts AI a hotkey away on macOS for selected text, though it is macOS-only and may need a VPN in some regions. [[link:/tools/262|AI Sidekick]] (Freemium) adapts to personal patterns but needs a paid plan for fuller features.

## Choosing guidance

If your team lives in Notion, start and stay with Notion AI. If you run projects in ClickUp, use ClickUp AI. If you are a Todoist user, add Mem or Obsidian for notes and Fireflies for meetings. Add Gamma or Tome when you present often, and Raycast if you are on Mac.

## A productivity workflow

Capture thoughts in Mem or Obsidian, plan in your task app, summarize meetings with Fireflies, draft decks in Gamma, and run quick commands with Raycast. Each tool owns one layer, so nothing is copied between five apps by hand.

## Common mistakes

The first mistake is adopting a tool whose context you do not feed, so it has nothing to work with. The second is paying for ClickUp AI or Notion AI without using the host app daily. The third is recording meetings without consent. The fourth is ignoring VPN access for region-locked tools. The fifth is expecting AI Sidekick to be useful before it learns your habits.

## FAQ

**Is Notion AI worth it outside Notion?** No; its value depends entirely on your notes living in Notion.

**Can ClickUp AI replace a separate notes app?** It helps within ClickUp, but pair it with Mem or Obsidian for general notes.

**How do I cover Todoist AI's gaps?** Add Fireflies for meetings and Mem or Obsidian for notes.

**Is Raycast AI available on Windows?** No, it is macOS-only.

**Why might a VPN be needed?** Several productivity tools restrict regional access, requiring a VPN in those areas.

## Pricing and access at a glance

Match the tier to your budget and confirm the tool works from your location before you build a workflow around it.
- [[link:/tools/5|Notion AI]] — Pricing: Freemium. Regional access may need a VPN in places.
- [[link:/tools/243|Mem]] — Pricing: Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/245|Obsidian]] — Pricing: Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/14|Obsidian Copilot]] — Pricing: Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/1106|Fireflies AI]] — Pricing: Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/240|Sembly AI]] — Pricing: Freemium.
- [[link:/tools/262|AI Sidekick]] — Pricing: Freemium.

Use the free tier as a filter: if it cannot handle one real project, paying will not fix the gap. Regional coverage is not fixed — verify it still applies where you work before you standardise on one tool.
tldr: Notion AI suits teams already in Notion, ClickUp AI suits teams in ClickUp, and Todoist AI users should pair it with note and meeting tools. Add Gamma, Fireflies, and Raycast for decks, capture, and commands.
